overview: The TB6600 is a step up from small pluggable drivers like the A4988 in every sense: a boxier standalone module rated for much larger stepper motors (NEMA 23/34 class, common in bigger CNC routers and industrial-adjacent builds), with screw terminals instead of solder pins and opto-isolated step/direction inputs that electrically separate the control signal from the motor power stage — protecting a microcontroller from motor-side electrical noise. Configuration is done with a bank of DIP switches for microstepping resolution and current limit, rather than a trimpot you adjust by feel.
simpleSummary: A rugged driver module for large stepper motors used in bigger CNC machines.

specifications.microstepping: Selectable via DIP switches: full step up to 1/32 step
specifications.motorCompatibility: 2-phase bipolar stepper motors, NEMA 17 through NEMA 34

pinMap.name: PUL+
pinMap.function: Step pulse input, positive side of the opto-isolated pair — each pulse moves the motor one (micro)step.

pinMap.name: DIR+
pinMap.function: Direction input, positive side — level sets rotation direction.

pinMap.name: ENA+
pinMap.function: Enable input, positive side — disabling cuts power to the motor coils, letting the shaft spin freely by hand.
pinMap.gotcha: Often left unconnected (motor enabled by default) — only wire it up if you specifically need free-spin/disable control.

pinMap.name: A+
pinMap.gotcha: Never disconnect motor wiring while powered — can spike-damage the driver.

useCases.title: CNC router/mill with larger steppers
useCases.scenario: Drive NEMA 23-class motors that exceed what a small A4988/DRV8825 module can safely handle.

useCases.title: Industrial-style positioning table
useCases.scenario: Opto-isolation makes it a safer choice near noisy industrial power electronics.

oftenConfusedWith: A4988/DRV8825 (smaller, lower current, no opto-isolation, direct microcontroller connection)
oftenUpgradedTo: Closed-loop stepper drivers (detect and correct missed steps)
